tips.title: Fixing Silvered Decals After They Have Dried
tips.text: Silvered decals happen when air is trapped under the decal. To fix after drying: apply Mr. Mark Softer generously over the decal, wait 10 minutes, then press gently with a damp cotton swab from the center outward to force air bubbles out. Repeat twice more with fresh solution. If silvering persists, carefully slit the decal film with a new #11 blade in a crosshatch pattern, apply setting solution again, and press flat. Once fully settled, seal with a gloss coat.

tips.title: Removing Old Paint from Plastic Kit Parts
tips.text: To remove old paint from plastic kit parts, submerge them in Vallejo Airbrush Thinner (or similar) for 15-30 minutes. Gently scrub with a soft toothbrush to loosen paint. Rinse with water and allow to dry. For stubborn areas, use a scalpel or dental pick to scrape off paint. Avoid using abrasive materials that could scratch the surface.

tips.title: Repairing Broken Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: To repair broken photo-etch parts, use CA (Cyanoacrylate) glue like Loctite Super Glue. Apply a small drop on the inside of the part, allowing it to wick into the break. Hold parts together for 30 seconds, then let dry completely. For added strength, apply a thin layer of Mr. Hobby Super Clear before drying. Sand any excess glue with a fine grit sanding stick.

tips.title: Recovering Clogged Airbrushes
tips.text: To recover a clogged airbrush, disassemble it and soak the nozzle, needle, and cap in an enzymatic cleaner like Iwata's Airbrush Cleaner for 15-30 minutes. Gently scrub with a soft brush, then rinse thoroughly with warm water. Reassemble the airbrush and test spray to ensure it's functioning properly. If clogs persist, use an airbrush cleaning pot or ultrasonic cleaner.

tips.title: Repairing Warped Plastic Parts
tips.text: To repair warped plastic parts, gently heat the warp using a hairdryer on low setting. Once softened, carefully bend the part back into shape. Hold it in place with small clamps or weights until cooled and hardened. For larger warps, use a heated block or hot water bath to soften the part, then bend and clamp into shape. Avoid overheating, as this can melt or damage the part.
